newsitem.title: UK: UK makes poor progress on youth skills - study.
newsitem.headline: UK makes poor progress on youth skills - study.

text.p: Britain made very little progress between 1985 and 1994 in reducing the proportion of 25 to 28-year-olds with low or no qualifications, according to a study published on Monday.
The Centre for Economic Performance, an independent research body based at the London School of Economics, said much greater progress had been made in France, Germany and Singapore.
"Britain still lags behind France and Germany in the proportion of young people reaching 'A-level' or equivalent," the study said.
"In France around two thirds of 18-year-olds reach that level; in Germany three-quarter do and even in Singapore half of 18-year-olds reach that level. In Britain the figure is 40 percent."
The study said fewer people in Britain and the United States had upgraded their skills from low to intermediate in the period compared with France and Germany.
